question: Carbonation creeps into concrete as the square root of time: 10 mm after 16 years. When does it reach steel 30 mm deep?
move: When progress slows as it goes, extra distance costs far more time.
trap: 48 years, tripling the time to triple the depth.
hint: Ask how much the time must grow for the depth to triple.
steps: Tripling the depth takes three squared, 9 times the time.
simply: Concrete keeps steel from rusting because it is strongly alkaline. Carbon dioxide from the air slowly neutralises it from the surface inward; when that front reaches the reinforcing bars, they start to rust, swell and push the concrete off.
reference: Neville, Properties of Concrete, 5th edition, Pearson, 2011
